discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 030749
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
249 AM EST Tue Nov 3 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Breezy and dry today with record-challenging warmth. Southerly
  wind gusts of 25 mph to perhaps 35 mph. 

- Rain arrives from west to east late tonight. Breezy with
  lingering showers through Wednesday.

- Not as warm to end the week with lake enhanced showers at
  times. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 249 AM EST Tue Nov 3 2026

A well defined upper-level trough is lifting north-northeast through 
Kansas early this morning. Closer to home, low stratus and patchy 
drizzle continues to lift north through Michigan in response to this 
lifting cyclone. Stout warm air advection has brought steadily 
rising temperatures on this shift with an increasing number of 60-
degree readings (normal high today is only 55). That said, morning 
temperatures will be a nice spring board for afternoon highs that 
will challenge the day's records: 76 degrees in 2003 and 1987 (2003 
record was only at Fort Wayne). Rather cloudy immediately upstream, 
but clearing is noted across the Ohio River. This could be enough 
later today to truly challenge the record. Cloud cover will also 
dictate afternoon mixing of the low-level jet. Forecast soundings 
depict a narrow window after 1pm where guidance attempts to mix down 
35 mph gusts. Overall today, breezy, decreasing clouds (especially 
along and east of the I-69 corridor) and dry. 

Rain slowly arrives from west to east Tuesday night according to 
available near-term models (RIP HREF, NAM et. al.). Northwest Ohio 
could very well be dry until after daybreak Wednesday as low 
pressure becomes stacked beneath the parent upper-low, slowing the 
cold front's arrival. Breezy conditions persist into Wednesday 
morning as the low-level jet remains amplified over northwest Ohio. 
A dry slot from this low slowly works its way east permitting some 
afternoon dry hours. Cooler air behind this system seeps in 
Wednesday night through Thursday along with lake-enhanced showers. 
Highs in the 60s Wednesday and Thursday give way to highs in the 50s 
Friday through the weekend. This whole system exits later Saturday 
ending the lake-enhanced shower chance.

Beyond the weekend, subtle northwest flow results in temperatures 
fairly close to normal and opportunities for 20% POPs at times as 
weak disturbances ripple through the flow. Subtle ridging is noted 
over the southern and central US, which, if building into the 
Midwest could later induce a more zonal flow locally. However, the 
core global models are teasing chilly Canadian High pressure after 
Veteran's Day. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 1149 PM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

Updated the 06z TAFs to reflect the lingering IFR ceilings which
are still anticipated to improve within the critical TAF 
period. Observations over north-central Indiana depict improving
conditions as the preexisting low-level moisture plume lifts 
northward in response an upper-level low lifts through Oklahoma.
Rain chances are best just beyond this TAF period. LLWS is 
increasingly marginal based on time- height cross sections, but
this carries on largely unchanged (delayed with the ceiling 
improvement).

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory from 7 AM this morning to 7 AM EST 
     Wednesday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

spc.text:
SPC AC 030534

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1134 PM CST Mon Nov 02 2026

   Valid 031200Z - 041200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   THE SABINE RIVER VALLEY INTO THE LOWER TO MID MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms with potential for isolated severe wind gusts and
   perhaps a brief tornado or two will be possible today from the
   Sabine and Lower Mississippi Valleys northward into the Mid
   Mississippi Valley.

   ...Sabine River Valley/Lower to Mid Mississippi Valley...
   An upper-level trough will move across the Great Plains today, as
   cyclonic south-southwesterly flow precedes the system over the lower
   to mid Mississippi Valley. Ahead of the system, a north-to-south
   corridor of low-level moisture will be in place along and ahead of a
   pre-frontal trough. Near the moist axis, a long broken line of
   thunderstorms will be ongoing at the start of the period from
   western Missouri southward into western Arkansas and east Texas.
   This line will progress eastward into the lower to mid Mississippi
   Valley during the day. As it does so, surface temperatures will warm
   ahead of the line allowing for weak destabilization. Any potential
   for moderate instability will be minimized by abundant cloud cover.
   Over the top of this airmass, moderate to strong deep-layer shear
   will be present, which will support an isolated severe threat during
   the afternoon and evening. Line segments that can become
   semi-organized will have potential for isolated severe wind gusts.
   In addition, a marginal tornado threat will be possible with any
   QLCS structures. The severe threat will be minimized by poor lapse
   rates. The threat could persist into the late evening or even into
   the overnight period as the line moves eastward across the lower to
   mid Mississippi Valley, toward a strengthening low-level jet.

   ..Broyles/Weinman.. 11/03/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.summary: Severe storms are unlikely on Wednesday.
spc.text:
SPC AC 030642

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1242 AM CST Tue Nov 03 2026

   Valid 041200Z - 051200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely on Wednesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A stacked low will move from IA into Upper MI on Wednesday, with a
   leading upper wave moving northeastward out of the OH Valley. Behind
   this system, another progressive shortwave trough will move across
   the Four Corners states. 

   As the surface low occludes and moves into the Upper Great Lakes,
   the southward-extending surface trough will weaken across the OH/TN
   Valleys. Mid to upper 60s F dewpoints will remain over much of the
   Southeast, with drier air farther north into the Mid Atlantic with
   high pressure. Scattered thunderstorms are likely during the day
   ahead of the boundary from KY southward into AL/GA, with poor lapse
   rates and the ejecting system to the north mitigating strong storm
   potential.

   There is a low chance of a few strong storms near a warm front that
   will lift across eastern AL into western GA during the day. At this
   time, it appears the very poor low to midlevel lapse rates will
   mitigate storm severity.

   ..Jewell.. 11/03/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 030810

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0210 AM CST Tue Nov 03 2026

   Valid 051200Z - 061200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely on Thursday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A shortwave trough will move across the central Plains and into the
   MS Valley where it will phase with the trough extending southward
   across the Great Lakes. This combined positive-tilt trough will then
   sweep eastward toward the OH and TN valleys overnight.

   Well ahead of this trough, southerly winds will bring 60s F
   dewpoints northward across the Mid Atlantic, though instability will
   be relatively weak. Isolated daytime convection may occur from GA
   into the Carolinas, but lapse rates and shear will both be poor.
   Scattered showers may persist overnight as a weak surface trough
   develops and southwest low-level winds maintain a moist air mass.

   ..Jewell.. 11/03/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
